title: Chapter 163: Wang Haiming's Secret
html:
“Why do you ask?” Xu Tong regretted the words immediately. One look at the hammer loosened his tongue again. “Wang Haiming was once a patient here. Repeated offenses sent him to the Third Sick Hall several times. He was an interesting man.”

“Be more specific.”

“He was low-risk and lived on the second floor of the second sick hall, but something was wrong with his mind. He kept insisting he wasn’t crazy.” A revolting smile spread across Xu Tong’s face. “We all know perfectly well that we’re normal. Only an idiot would feel the need to announce it.”

Chen Ge wondered how Wang Haiming would have felt being called an idiot by a diagnosed psychiatric patient. Malice flashed in Xu Tong’s smile. His view of reality differed completely from everyone else’s; perhaps even now, he believed himself perfectly healthy.

“What happened next?” Conversing with someone like Xu Tong was dangerous. Chen Ge had to guard against being drawn into the man’s private world and accepting its warped logic.

“Wang Haiming refused the hospital’s treatment. Whenever the staff tried to administer it, he fought the doctors and nurses.

“Attacking the staff was the worst possible offense here. The hospital punished him that very day.

“At first, they only confined him in an isolation room, but that made him worse. Once released, he fought a nurse after refusing his medication. He proclaimed himself a millionaire who could buy half the hospital and swore to make every doctor and nurse pay.

“Ten minutes later, the idiot paid for those words. The staff arrived with a straitjacket and transferred him to the Third Sick Hall’s isolation room.

“That was his first visit. We were delighted to welcome a new friend, but he proved very unfriendly—even spat at me. He looked full of energy and cursed without pause while they escorted him inside. The poor newcomer didn’t understand what the Third Sick Hall meant. He learned soon enough.

“Its isolation room had another name: the electroconvulsive therapy room. The doctors called it a common and remarkably effective treatment for mental illness.

“Naturally, as a licensed private hospital, they claimed to prioritize patient safety and comfort. An anesthesiologist assisted with the treatment, and the room was thoroughly soundproofed. Wang Haiming emerged much more obedient. We all agreed that the therapy had worked wonderfully.

“After several quiet days, Wang Haiming hid his medication and quarreled with the staff again. He possessed an instinct for adventure. Perhaps he truly had been a millionaire before his admission.

“When he emerged from isolation a second time, we assumed he would finally accept his fate. Instead, he planned a midnight escape—and, to everyone’s astonishment, succeeded. The staff caught him the following day, but during that one free night, he contacted his ex-wife. No one knows what he told her. Within a month, she arrived and arranged his discharge.”

Xu Tong’s account gave Chen Ge a much clearer picture of Wang Haiming. “How do you know so much about him?”

“After they recaptured him, the hospital confined him in Room 3 of the Third Sick Hall. He nearly died there, so the staff eventually had no choice but to place him with me temporarily.” Xu Tong’s twisted expression gradually relaxed.

“Then, do you know what happened to him in Room 3?”

“He saw many people. The room was full of them.”

“He told you that himself?” The mystery was growing more complicated. Wang Haiming had actually stayed in Room 3.

“Why would I speak to an idiot?” Xu Tong scoffed. “He muttered to himself every night. I overheard him.”

Chen Ge nodded. Only entering the Third Sick Hall himself would reveal the rest.

“Second question. Why did patients like you return after the hospital closed?”

“We each have our reasons. I can’t speak for the others, but I…” Xu Tong stared at him. “Only here can I escape your surveillance. Only here will you leave me alone.”

“It’s time for you to take your medicine.” Chen Ge stood up. He believed that Xu Tong did not lie to him.

The old man and young woman trembled at the sight of the one-armed man but showed no fear of Xu Tong. The old man had even dared bite him. Unlike the other two attackers, Xu Tong probably had not participated in their worst acts.

His cage was ruined from Chen Ge’s assault. Setting down the hammer, Chen Ge asked, “A female nurse was murdered inside the Third Sick Hall. Do you know about it?”

“Yes. The hospital held a memorial in the second sick hall, intending it as a lesson for patients, families, and staff.” Anticipating the next question, Xu Tong shrugged. “I had nothing to do with her death. The police questioned me. I stayed in my room that night, never spoke to her, and never saw her.”

Chen Ge nodded and asked about the hospital director, but Xu Tong knew little.

Within his limits, Xu Tong appeared truthful. His delusion made communication harder as the number of people around him increased; a crowd became one persecutor wearing many faces. Confined with only a few people, he could behave almost normally.

“I hope everything you said is true.” Chen Ge put both cameras back on and checked his phone.

Despite the long blackout, his audience had not fallen. It had surged past 150,000.

“What happened?” One look at the chat revealed his mistake: he had covered the cameras but left the microphone clipped to his lapel.

Xu Tong’s screams, the murdered nurse, Wang Haiming’s history, and the Third Sick Hall’s mysteries had all gone out live.

The accident sent his stream climbing even faster as the chat refreshed without pause.

“This is all too real!”

Likes and virtual gifts poured in.

For once, Chen Ge was speechless. Since matters had reached this point, he decided to abandon caution.

“Thank you for the gifts, the likes, and for joining me tonight.” He aimed the camera at himself. “What you’ve seen and heard may not be fiction. Tonight, I’ll bring you a livestream no one can ever recreate.”
